dedupe_keys.name: u s chemical safety board investigations

description: The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board is an independent federal agency that investigates major chemical incidents at fixed industrial facilities, and its investigations pages publish each case with location, incident date, status, investigation reports, factual updates, recommendations and videos. On 26 September 2026 current investigations included a fatal incident on 26 May 2026 at a packaging plant in Longview, Washington, a fatal hydrogen sulfide release on 22 April 2026 at a catalyst refinery in Institute, West Virginia, and a fatal toxic release in Baileyville, Maine, in February 2026. Coverage is the United States, per incident, with current and completed investigations. Access is free on the website with quick search and filters; reports are PDF documents, and as U.S. Government works they are in the public domain. Caveats: the Board investigates only a selection of serious incidents, so the collection is not a statistical sample, and reports are narrative documents, not a structured dataset. For simulation it provides detailed post-event analyses of refinery, chemical plant and process failures, useful for calibrating fault trees, cascading-failure and emergency response models. Related catalogue records include the EPA Toxics Release Inventory and the National Response Center incident data.
